themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 21 THIS WEEK, a 500% spike versus the 8-week baseline of 3.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.4), signaling a rapid deterioration in street homelessness visibility and safety concerns in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 21 encampment complaints filed last week vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score: 5.4)
Statistically significant spike indicates sudden clustering or expansion of encampments in the district
Community board has repeatedly requested park safety enhancements and security staff—chronic budget gap now materializing as visible street-level crisis
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations and interview residents and outreach workers about what triggered THIS WEEK's spike
Investigate whether a particular shelter closure, weather event, or enforcement policy change drove the sudden surge

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Jump
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped 51% THIS WEEK to 10 complaints versus a 6.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.94), suggesting emerging HVAC failures, mold issues, or CO concerns affecting housing stock amid cooling season demand.
evidence: 10 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (51% increase, z-score: 3.94)
Timing coincides with cooling season and high heat complaints (5,415 heat/hot water complaints in 90-day window—likely related system failures)
Suggests landlord neglect of building systems during peak demand period
reporting_angles: Interview Department of Health inspectors and residents to determine if spike is CO poisoning, mold, or HVAC breakdown
Cross-reference with heat complaint locations to identify buildings with cascading system failures

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Litter Streets
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded to 4 LAST WEEK, a 967% spike versus the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.49), indicating rapid accumulation of derelict bikes clogging sidewalks and indicating possible bike theft or scrappage operation.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
Converges with sidewalk condition spike (20 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 290%)—bikes are obstructing pedestrian access
Community board's repeated requests for litter basket collection and sidewalk maintenance suggest sanitation capacity gap
reporting_angles: Identify whether bikes are from bike-share system overspill, theft rings, or demolition of illegal vendors
Check with NYPD and Parks Enforcement for removal protocols and backlog

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Abuse Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 17 THREE WEEKS AGO (baseline 2.4 weekly), a 616% surge (z-score: 7.33), pointing to Uber/Lyft congestion, double-parking, or reckless driving concentrated in Washington Heights/Inwood corridors.
evidence: 17 for-hire vehicle complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (616% increase, z-score: 7.33)
Converges with illegal parking complaints (2,748 in 90 days, likely FHV double-parking) and street condition complaints
Pattern suggests neighborhood corridor(s) serving as pick-up/drop-off hub for outer-borough trips
reporting_angles: Identify which streets (Broadway, Amsterdam Ave, Dyckman St) are hotspots and interview residents about traffic/safety impact
Check TLC data for FHV density and driver compliance violations in the district

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Street Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints peaked at 20 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 290% jump versus the 5.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.75), reflecting accelerated pavement failure, trip hazards, and ADA access violations across the district.
evidence: 20 sidewalk condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (290% increase, z-score: 6.75)
Street condition complaints also elevated (669 total in 90 days)—signals systemic infrastructure backlog
Community board's recurring budget requests for street/park reconstruction indicate chronic unfunded maintenance, now manifesting as public safety hazard
reporting_angles: Walk affected blocks and photograph hazards; interview elderly residents and parents with strollers about fall/injury risks
Request DOT inspection data and replenish backlog queue to quantify borough-level repair wait times
